lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Ahaziah consults Baal-zebub and fire falls
nodes.d: Ahaziah, hurt in a fall, sends to ask Baal-zebub god of Ekron whether he will recover; Elijah meets the messengers and says he will die because there is a God in Israel. Fire from heaven consumes two captains of fifty, and Elijah goes with the third.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah sent Ahaziah this message and what happened to the soldiers?
ev: Say why Ahaziah was told he would die (1:3-4, 16)
Retell what happened to the captains of fifty

nodes.d: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?
ev: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear

nodes.t: Elijah is taken up and Elisha receives his mantle
nodes.d: Elijah and Elisha cross Jordan, Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, and Elijah is taken up by a whirlwind with a chariot of fire. Elisha takes up the fallen mantle, strikes the Jordan and crosses, and the sons of the prophets say the spirit of Elijah rests on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah left the earth and who took up his work?
ev: Describe how Elijah left and what Elisha picked up
Say what the sons of the prophets recognised (2:15)

nodes.t: Elisha heals the spring and the boys mock him
nodes.d: At Jericho Elisha casts salt into the spring and the waters are healed, according to his word; going up to Bethel, small boys mock him and two she bears tear forty-two of them after he curses them in the LORD's name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did at Jericho and what happened on the road to Bethel?
ev: Say what Elisha did to the waters at Jericho and by whose word
Describe what happened at Bethel (2:23-24)

nodes.t: Three kings and Moab: water in the valley
nodes.d: Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom march against rebel Moab and run out of water; Elisha, for Jehoshaphat's sake, says the LORD will fill the valley and give Moab into their hand. Water comes by morning and Moab is defeated, though the king of Moab offers his eldest son on the wall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD provided for the three kings, and why Elisha helped?
ev: Say why Elisha agreed to inquire of the LORD (3:13-14)
Describe how the water came (3:16-20)

nodes.d: A prophet's widow cries to Elisha because a creditor will take her two sons; Elisha tells her to borrow empty vessels and pour from her small pot of oil, and the oil flows until all the vessels are full, so she sells it and pays her debt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Elisha helped the widow pay her debt?
ev: Say what the widow had in the house and what happened to it
Say what she did with the oil afterwards (4:7)

nodes.d: A woman of Shunem builds a room for Elisha and, as he promised, bears a son; when the boy later dies, she goes to Elisha at Carmel, and Elisha prays, stretches himself on the child, and the boy sneezes and opens his eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the Shunammite's son was brought back to life?
ev: Say what the woman did for Elisha and what he promised her
Describe how Elisha restored the child

nodes.t: Death in the pot and the loaves
nodes.d: In a famine at Gilgal, wild gourds make the stew deadly and Elisha casts in meal so it is harmless; he then has a hundred men fed from twenty loaves, with some left, according to the LORD's word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did for the sons of the prophets during the famine?
ev: Say how Elisha made the pottage safe
Say what the LORD said about the twenty loaves (4:43)

nodes.d: Naaman, the Syrian commander, hears from an Israelite servant girl of the prophet in Samaria, goes to Elisha and is told to wash seven times in Jordan; he is angry but obeys and is healed, and confesses there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Gehazi takes a reward by deceit and Naaman's leprosy comes on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Naaman, the servant girl and Gehazi?
ev: Retell why Naaman was angry and what changed his mind
Say what happened to Gehazi and why (5:20-27)

nodes.d: While the sons of the prophets cut beams at Jordan, a borrowed axe head falls into the water; Elisha casts in a stick and the iron swims, and the man takes it up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to the borrowed axe head?
ev: Say what Elisha threw into the water and what happened
Say why the man was distressed (6:5)

nodes.t: Elisha and the Syrian army at Dothan
nodes.d: The king of Syria sends an army to take Elisha at Dothan; Elisha's servant sees them, Elisha prays and the servant sees chariots of fire around the mountain. The Syrians are struck blind, led to Samaria, given food and sent home, and the bands of Syria stop coming into Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha's servant saw at Dothan and how the story ended?
ev: Say what the servant saw when his eyes were opened (6:17)
Explain how Elisha told the king of Israel to treat the Syrians (6:21-23)

nodes.d: Benhadad besieges Samaria, a great famine follows and the king of Israel, hearing a woman's terrible plea, tears his clothes and swears to take Elisha's head; Elisha tells the elders the king's messenger is coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the famine in Samaria and how the king reacted?
ev: Describe the state of the city (6:25)
Say what the king blamed and decided (6:31, 33)

nodes.t: The LORD lifts the siege of Samaria
nodes.d: Elisha says that by tomorrow fine flour will sell for a shekel at the gate; four lepers find the Syrian camp empty because the LORD made the Syrians hear the noise of a great host, and the city is plundered. The lord who doubted sees it but dies in the gate trampled by the crowd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the siege of Samaria ended and how Elisha's word came true?
ev: Say what Elisha prophesied (7:1) and how it happened
Say what happened to the doubting lord (7:17-20)

nodes.t: The Shunammite's land and Elisha at Damascus
nodes.d: Elisha warns the Shunammite of a seven-year famine; on her return the king hears about Elisha's deeds from Gehazi and restores her land. Elisha later tells Hazael he will be king of Syria and do great evil to Israel, and Hazael kills Benhadad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the Shunammite woman after the famine, and what Elisha said to Hazael?
ev: Say what the king restored to the woman and why (8:4-6)
Say what Elisha told Hazael and how Elisha reacted (8:12)

nodes.d: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat marries a daughter of Ahab and does evil, yet the LORD will not destroy Judah for David's sake, as he promised David a light for his children. Edom revolts; his son Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab's house and goes with Joram of Israel to fight Hazael at Ramoth-gilead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God spared Judah despite Jehoram's evil?
ev: Say why the LORD did not destroy Judah (8:19)
Say how Jehoram and Ahaziah are compared to the house of Ahab (8:18, 27)

nodes.t: Jehu is anointed king over Israel
nodes.d: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to pour oil on Jehu's head and announce that he will strike the house of Ahab, and that dogs will eat Jezebel; the captains acclaim Jehu king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jehu was anointed and what he was told to do?
ev: Say what Jehu was told to do (9:6-10)
Describe how the other captains responded (9:13)

nodes.d: Jehu drives to Jezreel and shoots Joram, throwing him into Naboth's field according to the LORD's word; Ahaziah of Judah flees and is killed too.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joram and Ahaziah were killed?
ev: Say where Joram died and why Jehu cited Naboth (9:25-26)
Say what happened to Ahaziah of Judah

nodes.d: Jehu enters Jezreel; Jezebel is thrown from the window, trampled, and the dogs eat her, so that Jehu says it is the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah's word about Jezebel came true?
ev: Say how Jezebel died and what remained
Find the verse that links her death to Elijah's word (9:36)

nodes.t: Jehu destroys the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal
nodes.d: Jehu has Ahab's seventy sons killed in Samaria, kills Ahaziah's brethren and the remainder of Ahab's house, then gathers the worshippers of Baal in the house of Baal and has them slain, destroying the house and image of Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jehu did to Ahab's house and to Baal worship in Israel?
ev: Say how Jehu summoned the worshippers of Baal and what he did
Say whose word Jehu says is fulfilled (10:10)

nodes.d: The LORD tells Jehu that his sons to the fourth generation will sit on Israel's throne, but Jehu does not depart from Jeroboam's calves or walk in the law with all his heart, and the LORD begins to cut Israel short by Hazael.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain both the promise to Jehu and where he fell short?
ev: Say what the LORD promised Jehu and what Jehu failed to do (10:30-31)
Say who began to cut Israel short (10:32)

nodes.t: Athaliah and the hidden king Joash
nodes.d: After Ahaziah's death Athaliah destroys the royal seed and reigns six years; Jehosheba hides the baby Joash in the house of the LORD, and in the seventh year Jehoiada anoints him, Athaliah is put to death, and Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the king and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how young Joash became king of Judah?
ev: Say how Joash was saved and for how long he was hidden
Say what the covenant of Jehoiada was (11:17)

nodes.d: Joash does right while Jehoiada instructs him, though the high places stay; when the priests have not repaired the house by his twenty-third year, a chest is placed at the altar and the money repairs it. Hazael threatens Jerusalem and Joash is killed by his servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joash arranged the repair of the temple?
ev: Say how the temple money was collected and used (12:9-15)
Say how Joash's reign ended (12:17-21)

nodes.d: Jehoahaz of Israel follows Jeroboam's sins, so the LORD delivers Israel into Hazael's hand; when Jehoahaz seeks the LORD, he gives Israel a saviour, yet they do not depart from Jeroboam's sins. His son Joash reigns in the same way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD treated Israel under Jehoahaz?
ev: Say what happened when Jehoahaz sought the LORD (13:4-5)
Say whether Israel turned from Jeroboam's sins (13:6)

nodes.d: The dying Elisha has King Joash shoot an arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria and strike the ground; Joash strikes only three times, so Elisha says he will defeat Syria only three times. After Elisha's death a dead man touches his bones and revives; the LORD is gracious to Israel because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did on his deathbed and why the LORD still showed Israel compassion?
ev: Describe the arrows and why Elisha was angry (13:17-19)
Find the verse that names the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (13:23)

nodes.d: Amaziah does right, though not like David, kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children as the law of Moses says, defeats Edom, then challenges Joash of Israel and is beaten at Beth-shemesh, with Jerusalem's wall broken and the temple treasures taken. He is later killed in a conspiracy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Amaziah's reign, including his pride in challenging Israel?
ev: Say what Amaziah did and did not do with the children of the murderers (14:5-6)
Describe the result of his challenge to Israel (14:11-14)

nodes.d: Jeroboam son of Joash does evil like the earlier kings, yet restores Israel's border according to the word spoken by Jonah the prophet, because the LORD saw Israel's bitter affliction and had not said he would blot out Israel's name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD helped Israel by Jeroboam II even though he did evil?
ev: Name the prophet mentioned in 14:25
Say why the LORD saved Israel by Jeroboam (14:26-27)

nodes.d: Azariah (Uzziah) does right, but the high places remain and the LORD smites him with leprosy until his death; his son Jotham does right in the same way. In Jotham's days the LORD begins to send Rezin of Syria and Pekah against Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the reigns of Azariah and Jotham?
ev: Say what happened to Azariah and where he lived (15:5)
Say what remained in Judah despite the kings doing right (15:4, 35)

nodes.t: Israel's last kings: Zachariah to Pekah
nodes.d: Zachariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah and Pekah rule Israel in quick succession, mostly by conspiracy, all doing evil; Pul of Assyria is paid off by Menahem and Tiglath-pileser takes cities and carries people captive in Pekah's days. Hoshea then kills Pekah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Assyria began to take Israel's land and people?
ev: Say how Zachariah's end fulfilled the word to Jehu (15:12)
Say how Assyria begins to affect Israel (15:19, 29)

nodes.t: Ahaz of Judah turns to Assyria
nodes.d: Ahaz walks in the way of Israel's kings, burns his son in the fire and sacrifices at the high places. Rezin and Pekah besiege Jerusalem, and Ahaz sends the temple silver and gold to Tiglath-pileser; he then copies a Damascus altar and moves the LORD's bronze altar aside.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Ahaz did instead of trusting the LORD when Syria and Israel attacked?
ev: Say who Ahaz asked for help and what he paid (16:7-8)
Describe what he did with the altar at the temple (16:10-16)

nodes.d: Hoshea becomes Assyria's servant, then conspires with Egypt; Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, takes it in Hoshea's ninth year and carries Israel into Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how and when the northern kingdom of Israel was taken captive?
ev: Say what Hoshea did that led to the siege (17:4)
Say where Israel was carried (17:6)

nodes.d: The writer explains that Israel sinned against the LORD who brought them from Egypt, walked in the nations' ways, ignored the prophets, rejected his covenant and statutes, and followed Jeroboam's sin, so the LORD removed them. Judah also did not keep his commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give the reasons 2 Kings 17 gives for Israel's exile?
ev: List several sins named in 17:7-17
Say how the LORD had warned them (17:13)

nodes.d: The king of Assyria brings peoples from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath and Sepharvaim to Samaria; lions come among them until a priest taught the manner of the God of the land, but each nation keeps its own gods while also fearing the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened in the land after Israel was taken away?
ev: Say how the settlers came to fear the LORD (17:25-28)
Say why the writer says they did not truly fear the LORD (17:34-41)

nodes.d: Hezekiah does right as David did, removes the high places and breaks the bronze serpent Moses made, which Israel had been burning incense to, and trusts the LORD like no king before or after him. He rebels against Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what made Hezekiah a good king?
ev: Say what Hezekiah removed and what he did to the bronze serpent (18:4)
Say what the writer says about his trust in the LORD (18:5-7)

nodes.d: Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities and Hezekiah pays him; the king of Assyria still sends Rabshakeh, who mocks Hezekiah's trust in the LORD and Egypt and tells the people not to listen to him, asking which gods have delivered their land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Rabshakeh said to shake Judah's trust in the LORD?
ev: Say what Rabshakeh told the people on the wall (18:28-35)
Say how the people responded (18:36)

nodes.d: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prays; Isaiah says the LORD will defend the city for his own sake and David's sake, and that night the angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his sons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God answered Hezekiah's prayer against Sennacherib?
ev: Retell Hezekiah's prayer and what he asked (19:15-19)
Say what happened to the Assyrian army (19:35)

nodes.t: Hezekiah's illness and the Babylonian envoys
nodes.d: Hezekiah is told by Isaiah he will die, prays, and the LORD adds fifteen years, giving the shadow going back ten degrees as a sign. Afterward he shows Babylon's envoys all his treasures, and Isaiah tells him all will be carried to Babylon; Hezekiah says the word is good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD did when Hezekiah was sick, and what Isaiah said about Babylon?
ev: Say what sign the LORD gave and what he promised (20:5-11)
Say what Isaiah foretold about Babylon (20:16-18)

nodes.d: Manasseh rebuilds the high places, sets altars for the host of heaven in the LORD's house, passes his son through the fire and sheds much innocent blood; the LORD announces evil on Jerusalem like Samaria's. His son Amon does the same and is killed by his servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Manasseh led Judah further into sin, and what the LORD announced?
ev: List some of Manasseh's sins (21:3-6, 16)
Say what the LORD announced would happen to Jerusalem (21:12-15)

nodes.t: Josiah and the book of the law
nodes.d: In Josiah's eighteenth year, repairs to the temple turn up the book of the law; the king tears his clothes at its words, and Huldah the prophetess says the evil will come on Jerusalem but not in Josiah's days because his heart was tender.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the book of the law was found in the temple?
ev: Say what Hilkiah found and how Josiah reacted (22:8-11)
Say what Huldah told Josiah (22:16-20)

nodes.t: Josiah renews the covenant and cleanses the land
nodes.d: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to walk after him; he removes idols and high places in Judah, defiles Topheth, and at Bethel breaks Jeroboam's altar and burns bones on it according to the word of the man of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Josiah renewed the covenant and what he removed?
ev: Say what Josiah covenanted (23:3)
Describe what he did at Bethel and which earlier prophecy it matched (23:15-18)

nodes.t: Josiah's Passover and the verdict on Judah
nodes.d: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover as written; no such Passover had been held since the judges. No king before or after turned to the LORD as he did, yet the LORD did not turn from his wrath because of Manasseh, and says he will remove Judah as he removed Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD still would not turn from his anger after Josiah's reforms?
ev: Say how the Passover was different (23:22)
Say why the LORD did not turn from his wrath (23:26-27)

nodes.t: Josiah's death and Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
nodes.d: Josiah dies at Megiddo when Pharaoh-nechoh goes up to Assyria; Jehoahaz reigns three months and is taken to Egypt, and Pharaoh makes Eliakim king as Jehoiakim, who taxes the land to pay him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Judah's kings right after Josiah?
ev: Say how Josiah died (23:29-30)
Say who appointed Jehoiakim (23:34)

nodes.d: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar, then rebels, and the LORD sends bands against Judah as he said by the prophets because of Manasseh's sin; his son Jehoiachin surrenders to Babylon and Nebuchadnezzar carries off the temple treasures and about ten thousand captives. He appoints Zedekiah king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Babylon took the first captives from Judah?
ev: Say why the LORD sent the invaders (24:2-4)
Say what Nebuchadnezzar took and who he made king (24:13-17)

nodes.d: Zedekiah rebels and Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem; the city is broken up, Zedekiah is blinded after his sons are killed, and the Chaldeans burn the temple, palace and houses, break the walls and carry off the temple's bronze and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how and why Jerusalem was destroyed?
ev: Describe what happened to Zedekiah and to the temple
Say how Judah's exile is summed up (25:21)

nodes.d: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah, but Ishmael kills him and the people flee to Egypt. The book ends with Evil-merodach lifting Jehoiachin out of prison in Babylon and giving him a daily allowance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how 2 Kings ends and who was released from prison?
ev: Say what happened to Gedaliah (25:25)
Say how the book of 2 Kings ends (25:27-30)

nodes.d: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?
ev: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)

nodes.t: The man of God from Judah and the old prophet
nodes.d: A man of God from Judah cries against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, naming a child Josiah, and the altar is rent. He is told not to eat or drink there, but is deceived by an old prophet and killed by a lion on the way home.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the man of God who came from Judah to Bethel?
ev: Retell how the man of God disobeyed and what happened
Say what the sign at the altar was (13:3-5)

nodes.d: The widow's son falls sick and dies; Elijah prays and stretches himself on the child, the LORD hears and the child revives. The woman says she now knows Elijah is a man of God and the LORD's word in his mouth is truth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the widow's son was brought back to life and what she said?
ev: Retell what Elijah did and prayed
Say what the widow confessed at the end (17:24)

nodes.t: The LORD speaks to Elijah at Horeb
nodes.d: At Horeb Elijah complains that he alone is left; the LORD is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and sends him to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, saying he has left seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Elijah at Horeb and how he spoke?
ev: Describe the wind, earthquake, fire and voice
State the three people Elijah was told to anoint and the number left in Israel

nodes.d: The LORD sends Elijah to Ahab in Naboth's vineyard: Ahab's house will be cut off like Jeroboam's and Baasha's and the dogs will eat Jezebel. Ahab tears his clothes and humbles himself, and the LORD says the evil will not come in his days but in his son's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab about Naboth's vineyard and what happened when Ahab humbled himself?
ev: State the judgment on Ahab and on Jezebel (21:21-24)
Say how the LORD responded when Ahab humbled himself (21:27-29)

nodes.d: 1 Chronicles opens with genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles (chs. 1-9), tells of Saul's death and David's reign (chs. 10-21), and then David's preparations for the temple, the organising of Levites and officers, and the accession of Solomon (chs. 22-29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Chronicles in order, from the genealogies to David's death?
ev: Name the three parts: genealogies, David's reign, preparations for the temple
Say how the book begins (Adam) and ends (David's death and Solomon reigning)

nodes.t: Jehoiada crowns Joash and Athaliah is slain
nodes.d: In the seventh year Jehoiada makes a covenant with the captains, brings out the king's son in the temple with guards and Levites, anoints him, and Athaliah is put to death; Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the people and the king, and the house of Baal is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Joash became king and how the people renewed their covenant?
ev: Say how Joash was crowned and who protected him (23:1-11)
State what the king's son reigning is said to fulfil (23:3)

nodes.d: Amaziah obeys the law about not killing children for fathers' sins, sends away hired Israelite troops at a prophet's word and defeats Edom, but then brings home Edom's gods and worships them. He ignores the prophet, challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth-shemesh, and is later killed in a conspiracy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Amaziah went from obeying the LORD to worshipping idols?
ev: Say what Amaziah did after defeating Edom (25:14)
Say why God was angry and what resulted (25:15-24)

nodes.t: Sennacherib threatens and the LORD delivers Jerusalem
nodes.d: Sennacherib invades Judah; Hezekiah strengthens Jerusalem and tells the people there is more with them than with the king of Assyria. Sennacherib's servants mock the LORD, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and the LORD sends an angel to cut off the Assyrian leaders; Sennacherib goes home and his sons kill him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, and what God did?
ev: Say what Hezekiah told the people (32:7-8)
Say what the LORD did after Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed (32:20-22)

nodes.t: The book of the law found and the covenant renewed
nodes.d: Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the temple; Josiah tears his clothes, sends to Huldah the prophetess, who says the evil will come but not in his days because he humbled himself. Josiah reads the book to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to keep his commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the book of the law was found and what Josiah did next?
ev: Say what Josiah did when the book was read (34:19)
Say what Huldah told him and what covenant he made (34:23-31)

nodes.d: Pharaoh Necho goes up to fight at Carchemish and warns Josiah not to meddle, saying God commanded him; Josiah does not heed and goes out to fight at Megiddo, where archers wound him, and he dies; all Judah mourns, and Jeremiah laments for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Josiah died and who mourned for him?
ev: Say what Necho told Josiah (35:21)
Say what Josiah did and what happened (35:22-24)

nodes.d: Esther tells how a Jewish orphan becomes queen of Persia, Haman plots to destroy the Jews, Esther and Mordecai act, the plot is reversed, and the feast of Purim is established. The name of God does not appear in the book.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Esther from Vashti's removal to the feast of Purim?
ev: Say who the main people are: Ahasuerus, Esther, Mordecai and Haman
Say what the feast of Purim remembers

nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.d: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads the passage about the anointed preacher of good news and says it is fulfilled in their hearing; he points to Elias and Eliseus helping outsiders, and the crowd tries to throw him down.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus read in Nazareth and why the people were angry?
ev: Say what Jesus read, what he said about it, and why the people turned on him.
